old: Its name secretly points to a region on the map, not to how many floors it has.
It comes from a Gujarati word for a house built in the style of a particular eastern homeland.
It's a doublet of Bangla and bangalo — cousins all tracing back to Bengal.
clues: This kind of house hides the name of a whole region inside it: it began as a word for a home built in the style of Bengal.
Today it names a modest detached house with all its rooms on a single floor, smaller and cozier than a sprawling ranch house, and often favored by retirees.
Picture a Craftsman-style one with a deep front porch, or a British seaside holiday rental. It shares its origin with the word Bangla.
